This is in line with both Gandhi and one of the foremost scholars on power, Michel Foucault. To Gandhi, “exploitation” is at the core of violence (Gandhi 1942: 258), and to Foucault “domination” is the ethical problem with power (Vinthagen 2006). Power itself is, according to Foucault,
an interactive relationship of social forces

that shifts and involves a dynamic struggle, whereas domination is the frozen hierarchy of subordination of some people or behavior, which stops (or is trying to stop) dynamic change and struggle, i.e., structures that determine our life quality and potential to live (Foucault 1982: 790; Lilja and Vinthagen 2014; Vinthagen 2006).
